mcp.tool.runtimeServiceDescriptor: Return the local runtime service descriptor and exact current instance identity. This grants no shutdown permission.
mcp.tool.shutdownRuntimeService: Admit a policy-authorized shutdown for the exact service and instance. Acceptance does not mean the service has stopped.
mcp.tool.listDeclaredModels: List configured model declarations. This does not observe provider availability, credentials, activation, or execution readiness.
config.field.provider_catalog: Versioned native provider and model declarations; not activation or availability.
mcp.tool.inspectModelBinding: Inspect one exact configured model declaration and its semantic binding digest. This does not observe availability, credentials, activation, or execution readiness.
mcp.tool.inspectModelActivation: Inspect scoped recorded model activation. This does not establish provider availability or invocation permission.
mcp.tool.admitModelActivation: Explicitly activate or deactivate an exact model under current policy. An idempotent replay returns historical evidence, not current state; no provider is invoked.
mcp.tool.inspectModelCatalog: List the ledger model catalog as one scope sees it: channels, exact model ids, lifecycle, CLI minimum and activation. Read only.
mcp.tool.applyModelCatalog: Register catalog facts (installation-wide authority) or activate/deactivate a channel or exact model in one scope. A replayed command id returns its receipt without a second change.
mcp.tool.inspectPoolHold: Show the execution pool's typed hold: held or open, who changed it and why, reserved/running and evaluating occupancy, and drained (held with nothing left). Read only.
mcp.tool.applyPoolHold: Hold or resume an execution pool installation-wide (installation-level authority): while held no new task is reserved, running work finishes and is evaluated, Run admission stays open. A replayed command id returns its receipt without a second change.
config.field.provider_invocation_profile: Native invocation profiles and explicit request allocations
config.field.provider_spending: Scope-specific model spending budgets and reservation limits
config.field.provider_spend_audit: Optional bounded provider-spending audit page, reservation, and time limits
mcp.tool.inspectModelInvocation: Inspect a persisted model invocation with current authorization. It requires an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`; a runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects. Response content is withheld by default; JSON includeResponseContent additionally requires inspect-content permission, and human output never shows retained response content.
mcp.tool.purgeModelInvocationContent: Purge active retained native, usage, or raw response content by exact command identity and expected content digest. Requires the local runtime service and separate purge-content policy authorization. It preserves the invocation outcome, quota record, and no-resend identity; logical purge does not erase write-ahead logs, media, or backups.
mcp.tool.cancelModelInvocation: Record cancellation intent for an exact model invocation command. It may prevent local dispatch before send permission; after permission it does not claim remote cancellation or completion.
mcp.tool.invokeModel: Submit one native model request using the configured profile and durable command identity. It requires an explicitly started local `deckent runtime serve`; a runtime-owned invocation continues if the client disconnects. Retrying the same command identity returns its receipt and does not resend the native request. Complete result capacity is checked before a new call. A received native response or rejection is evidence only, neither task acceptance nor a billing determination; the lifetime call is consumed.
mcp.error.modelInvocationResultLimit: The complete result cannot fit this MCP surface. Increase its configured response capacity. For an existing invocation, use SDK or CLI inspection to retrieve the saved result; do not submit a new command to repeat the model call.
mcp.tool.inspectProviderSpending: Inspect one exact scoped provider-spending account snapshot. It returns recorded local reservations, including holds but not hold reasons, and exact settlement with its rounded projection. The settled total may combine local calculations and provider-reported charges; source subtotals are not included. It does not verify a provider invoice or a full spending-history audit.
mcp.tool.auditProviderSpending: Record one bounded integrity audit for an exact provider-spending checkpoint. It creates or replays an immutable audit receipt; it does not correct financial records, verify a provider invoice, or prove a complete invocation audit.
cli.coding.help:
deckent coding [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Lists the coding profiles task kinds run on (kind · profile · provider · CLI · image) and the configured worker image.
deckent coding template [--provider <id>] [--kind <kind>] [--image <sha256>] [--preview|--apply] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Preview or add a validated reusable coding template through governed configuration; existing kind bindings are preserved. On a terminal the missing choices are asked (admitted provider, task kind, admitted image) and a preview card is confirmed before writing; elsewhere --provider, --kind and --preview|--apply are required and a missing choice lists the admitted values.
deckent coding prepare --input <file|-> [--json] [--lang en|tr]
Prepare a native coding Docker profile; does not start a worker or change configuration. Input fields: schemaVersion 1, template (an execution profile) and invocation (a native coding invocation); the first field that does not fit is named.
cli.workers.help:
Usage: deckent workers [list|watch] [--scope <id>] [--all | --since <12h>] [--verbose] [--limit <n>] [--samples <n>] [--json]
Shows the workers that are running or need attention now (default scope when --scope is not given), one row each.
--all / --since 12h  include finished workers   --verbose  per-source detail   --json  the full observation report
watch: one live window on a terminal (Esc or q closes); in a pipe it prints snapshots.
To follow work live, use deckent monitor.
cli.operation.help:
Usage: deckent operation [--json] [--lang en|tr]   the operation catalog of this installation (operation · target · effect · approval · compensation)
  operation execute|compensate --input <file|-> [--wait <ms>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
  operation execute --schema   the input contract (JSON Schema)
  operation inspect --scope <id> --command-id <id> [--json]   exit 1 when no operation is recorded (--json: record null)
Input fields: schemaVersion 1, commandId, scopeId, operation {id, version}, target {kind, id}, idempotencyKey, input and expectedVersion (or null); the full contract is `deckent operation execute --schema`.
Runs a catalog operation (operations config) against its declared target: conditional write on the expected record version, idempotency key, intent recorded before the effect. Unknown outcomes are not retried; compensation is a new operation. An operation that requires approval reports the open approval request (status approval-pending) and sends nothing; decide it with `deckent approval decide`, then resubmit the same command. --wait polls the decision up to the given milliseconds and resubmits once after an allow. A document that is not an operation command names its field and sends nothing.

cli.monitor.help:
monitor [--once|--json] [--verbose] [--install <id>] [--scope <id>] [--lang en|tr] [--no-color]
Watch every observed install in one place: Runs and why they are stuck, workers, approvals waiting for you, pools and builds.
On a terminal it opens a fullscreen view refreshed every inspection.workers.heartbeatMs (q quits, ? shows keys).
--once prints one plain-text snapshot (also when piped); --json prints the snapshot as JSON. Observe only.
Config: tab 8 reads the current project configuration; --config [--once|--json] prints it without worker reads.
--install current|<id> collects only the selected installation; other sources are not opened. JSON sourcesRead lists collection targets attempted, including denied or unavailable sources.
--verbose lists every refused or failed scope by name (text and window show the first few, then a count) and adds every worker's detail (report, transcript, task text) to --once; JSON always lists all.
